# Stand Firm in the Gap
## Scripture
"Watch, stand fast in the faith, be brave, be strong." – 1 Corinthians 16:13

## Reflection
Paul’s closing words to the Corinthians read like a commander’s final orders before battle. He doesn’t tell us to attack, retreat, or negotiate. He tells us to *stand*. In a culture that glorifies constant motion and aggressive advancement, standing firm feels passive. But in the spiritual realm, standing is the most aggressive posture of faith. It means your foundation is settled, your identity is secure, and your enemy cannot move you.

Men, we are called to be the gap-standers—the ones who hold the line when everything else shakes. Your family, your workplace, your church need a man who will not fold under pressure or compromise under comfort. Bravery isn't the absence of fear; it's the refusal to let fear dictate your obedience. Strength isn't muscle; it's the disciplined will to remain faithful when it would be easier to walk away.

Today, check your posture. Are you standing in Christ, or are you swaying with the wind of circumstance? Anchor yourself in His truth, and hold the line.

## Daily Challenge
Do 25 pushups today. On each pushup, say aloud: "I stand firm in the faith." Let your body remind your spirit of your resolve.
